correctness.rationale: Setting \(\\\(\\gamma=0\\)\) in equations (4.6a)–(4.6b) makes the discriminant \(|\alpha\beta-4|\), yielding exactly the unordered pair \(\{\sqrt2/\alpha,\beta/(2\sqrt2)\}\). Theorem 6.2 classifies each channel at \(\mu<1\), \(\mu=1\), and \(\mu>1\), while Theorem 6.3 adds the free branch. Theorem 7.2 differs from the sum of the two Jacobi counts by at most two, and the asymptotic used in Theorem 7.3 converts to the displayed coordinate inverse-square-root terms. The bounded error is negligible because their sum diverges for every interior approach to the corner.

value.rationale: The slice \(\\\(\\gamma=0\\)\) is the natural no-mixing subfamily of the full contact interaction and simultaneously contains the two canonical transition mechanisms. The result gives a complete two-parameter phase classification, identifies two independent critical lines and their bicritical intersection, distinguishes the label-swap curve \(\alpha\beta=4\) from true phase boundaries, and gives a path-independent additive divergence law near the corner. This is a structural classification rather than a routine numerical specialization.
